zh.title: 这个一人公司的 AI 每月赚 6.9 万美元！Fastlane 把网址变成宣传短视频，帮你做营销推广
zh.excerpt: 收入数字来自创始人自报，Fastlane 也是团队项目。更值得研究的，是它怎样把网址、素材、发布与反馈接成持续工作流。
zh.content:
我目前已经上架了 6 个苹果 App，也为它们准备了 H5 体验入口。做出产品之后，我遇到的一个大问题是：不会推广。

怎么让别人看见？看见之后，怎么让他知道这个产品与自己有关？这些问题，比再增加一个功能更需要我认真面对。

最近研究的 Fastlane，恰好从这里切入。它让我感兴趣的，是把推广接成一套可以反复运行的工作流。

![上架了 6 个 App，却卡在推广。Fastlane 给我的启发。](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/01-shipped-six-apps.png)

## 01｜上架之后，还有另一半工作

在 WonderElian 的「沿途所作」里，你能看到一休冥想、不二见己、三慢问道、虾子曰、艺术风格图鉴等作品。[1]

我知道自己为什么做它们。但一个第一次遇见产品的人，不会自动拥有这些背景。他可能不知道有什么用，可能没有耐心看完整页介绍，也可能暂时没有相关需要。

因此，推广要回答一个很具体的问题：你在什么时刻，会想起它？

一个忙到睡前还停不下来的人，与一个困在麻烦人际关系中的人，需要的表达、入口和理由显然不同。把功能列表写得更完整，并不能代替这一步。

## 02｜他也经历过“做出来，却难以被看见”

Fastlane 联合创始人 Gaurav 在访谈里说，自己做过几个 App，随后卡在营销上。他与同伴围绕这个问题创业。[2]

![他也做过 App，也卡在推广。Fastlane 从这个反复发生的痛点里长起来。](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/02-marketing-bottleneck.png)

在 2026 年 8 月 30 日发布的访谈中，他披露软件业务月度经常性收入约 6.9 万美元，付费用户超过 1,000 人。这是创始人自报数据，不等于净利润，也不代表今天的实时收入。[2]

Product Hunt 页面可核实其 2026 年 3 月 23 日发布时获得当日第 3 名。[3]

这个案例有商业吸引力，但它本身是团队创业，不能被包装成“一个人随便做个工具就能月入这么多”。对我更有价值的，是它找到了一个我也正在经历、而且会反复发生的问题。

## 03｜它怎样把推广接起来？

目前官网展示的 Fastlane v2，由名为 Senna 的 AI 代理串联五个环节：从网址理解品牌，研究市场，生成素材，发布内容，再根据结果调整下一批。[4]

![把产品网址，变成营销工作流。理解产品、研究市场、生成素材、发布与试验。](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/03-url-to-workflow.png)

官网呈现的渠道包括 Meta、Instagram、TikTok 和 YouTube Shorts。这些是官方介绍的能力范围；实际可用性仍取决于套餐、账号接入与具体功能。[4]

我的 H5 入口，在这里可能是一个优势。创始人在 Product Hunt 回应移动 App 开发者时，建议优先提供信息更充分的网站。[3]

不过，一个首页如果只讲品牌故事，没有明确用户、场景和产品价值，AI 也只能在模糊的信息上继续生成。输入网址只是起点。我仍要把“给谁用、解决什么、下一步怎么体验”讲清楚。

## 04｜我最喜欢的设计：让人从选择开始

早期 Fastlane 演示里，用户可以像左右滑动卡片一样筛选素材，再安排发布。[2]

![先生成，再筛选。把“从零创作”的难题，变成“要不要用”的选择。](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/04-generate-then-choose.png)

这个设计让我觉得很聪明。

面对空白编辑器，我需要自己决定选题、开头、形式和表达。面对已经做好的几个候选，我可以先判断：这条像我吗？有没有讲清楚？我愿不愿意把它发出去？

AI 承担前面的制作，人保留最后的选择。这降低了开始做营销的门槛，也让审美、语气和诚实的产品表达有了落脚点。

如果我做自己的推广工具，会认真借鉴这个原则。具体界面可以不同，关键是让我更容易完成一次有质量的发布。

## 05｜这门生意，为什么能持续收费？

App 上线之后，还要不断解释价值、测试表达、触达新用户。这样的需求，天然会重复发生。

![推广是持续发生的需要。订阅、生成额度与服务，围绕它展开。](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/05-recurring-marketing.png)

截至 2026 年 10 月 14 日，官网显示的主要套餐如下，均为美元、未含可能适用的税费：[4][5]

**Starter**：月付 $29；年付折算每月 $20；每月 500 credits。

**Growth**：月付 $79；年付折算每月 $55；每月 2,000 credits。

**Pro**：月付 $199；年付折算每月 $139；每月 10,000 credits。

年付折算对应全年预付，不能按这个折算价逐月付款。官网标注静态素材消耗 5 credits、视频 60 credits；Starter 还有 1 个社交账号、同时 1 个 campaign 的限制。[4]

这里的商业逻辑分三层：订阅对应持续使用，额度对应不同强度的生成，额外服务对应用户希望进一步省心的需求。

我的理解是，额度也给生成成本留出了控制空间。不过，公开资料不足以计算它的真实毛利、获客成本和用户流失率。收入数字只能帮助我们看见需求，不能直接说明这门生意有多轻松。

对我这 6 个 App 而言，账号、campaign 和工作空间限制，也要一起算。付费投放还需要另外的预算；额外账号与代运营服务也会增加成本。要比较的，是完成一次有效推广的总成本。

还有一个影响试用的细节：官网写 7 天试用 50 credits，而一条视频需要 60 credits。因此，不能默认试用额度足够生成视频；具体赠送方式和视频体验资格，需要在试用前确认。[4]

## 06｜值得学的，还有它怎样理解用户

访谈里，团队介绍了用额外使用时间邀请用户通话，并把反馈整理成产品决策依据的方法。[2]

![真正决定产品方向的，是用户怎么使用，为什么愿意继续使用。](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/06-real-direction.png)

对我而言，真正值得带走的是三种不同的观察：先了解人们现在怎样解决问题，再看他们实际怎么使用产品，最后了解哪些人持续回来、为什么回来。

“你觉得我的产品好吗？”很容易换来一句客气的肯定。真正有用的问题往往更具体：你上一次遇到这个问题是什么时候？用了什么办法？哪一步最费劲？

如果将来把自己的推广系统分享出去，我希望先观察别人怎样用，而不是急着补上一堆自己想象中的功能。

## 07｜它能接住我的哪些工作？

从公开介绍来看，Fastlane 与我的需求是相符的：已有产品网址，需要持续制作推广内容，又希望降低制作和分发的负担。

![我的 6 个 App，不能只靠同一种话术。先找到每个产品、每个真正需要被解决的时刻。](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/07-one-loop.png)

它目前公开列出的主要是海外渠道。如果要做公众号、视频号、小红书或抖音，它不支持。海外版本值得试，国内的内容与分发方式还需要另行验证。

但 6 个 App 意味着不同的用户需要。推广一休，可以从“午后怎样给自己一个短暂休息”开始；推广艺术风格图鉴，可以从“为什么这张图看起来更有秩序”开始。这些是我想测试的表达方向，不是已经验证的增长结论。

素材生成可以交给 AI，产品里的真实体验仍要讲准确。不能把尚未上线的功能放进宣传，也不能用虚构的用户评价证明价值。Fastlane 条款同样要求人工审查，并说明生成内容不保证完全独特或没有第三方权利问题。[5]

官网里的高播放案例会吸引我。但对我的 App，更重要的判断是：有没有人因此进入 H5、完成一次体验、下载 App，或愿意付费。播放量只是其中一个环节。

## 08｜如果自己做，我想从一个小循环开始

我的想法是，先满足自己的需要，打磨到真正用得起来，再分享给身边有相似问题的人。

![我想先给自己做一套，真正用得起来的推广系统。从一个 App、一个渠道、一次真实反馈开始。](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/08-build-one-loop.png)

第一版可以很小：先选一个 App 和一个渠道，整理好产品信息，让 AI 提供几个内容方向；我挑选并修改，再安排发布；把结果带回下一次选题。

已有 H5，可以作为低门槛的体验入口。每条内容使用可区分来源的链接，观察访问和实际使用。App Store 按钮点击、真实下载、激活与付费需要分别看，不能当成同一个数字。

我也想记录另一件事：这套系统，每周究竟替我省了多少工作？如果它只生产了更多待审核素材，最后仍让我越来越忙，就没有解决我的问题。

至于将来怎样收费，应该等持续价值出现以后再判断。有人长期需要规划、生成、排期和复盘，订阅才有理由；偶尔需要一次交付的人，也许更适合按次付费。

先把一条路走通，再考虑把它铺得更宽。

## 09｜我想让需要这些作品的人看见它们

Fastlane 让我看见了一个值得认真研究的方向：创作与推广之间，可以有一套更容易坚持的工作方法。

![先解决自己的痛点。打磨好，再分享给需要的人。](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/09-refine-and-share.png)

我做这些 App，是因为自己有需要，也相信生活里有些问题值得被认真照顾。如今我想补上的，是把它们介绍给合适的人。

先解决自己的痛点，把真实使用里的困难一件件磨掉。有一天，如果它也能帮到身边的人，我会很愿意分享。

我想把作品做出来，也想让需要它的人看见。

本期采用[虾子曰艺术风格图鉴](https://style-atlas.wonderelian.com/)推荐的 **Fractal Art／分形艺术风格**。递归分支、筛选与回流表现产品传播和反馈，让复杂的推广过程变得可以观察、选择与迭代。

### 参考资料

- [WonderElian「沿途所作」](https://wonderelian.com/)；文中 6 个已上架苹果 App 的数量由作者提供。
- [Starter Story: The Insanely Obvious Secret Behind This $69K/Month SaaS](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/the-insanely-obvious-secret-behind-this-69k-month-saas)，2026 年 8 月 30 日发布；收入与用户数为访谈自报口径。
- [Product Hunt：Fastlane](https://www.producthunt.com/products/fastlane-3)，用于发布记录及联合创始人的公开答复。
- [Fastlane 官网](https://www.usefastlane.ai/)，功能、价格、额度与渠道于 2026 年 10 月 14 日查看；官网演示与客户案例不构成个人效果保证。
- [Fastlane 服务条款](https://www.usefastlane.ai/terms)，用于人工审查、生成内容与费用说明。

en.label: Field Notes
en.title: This AI SaaS Makes $69K a Month: How Fastlane Turns a Website into a Marketing Workflow
en.excerpt: The revenue is founder-reported and Fastlane is a team venture. The useful lesson is how it connects a URL, creative production, publishing, and feedback.
en.content:
I currently have six apps on Apple’s App Store, and I have also prepared H5 web experiences for them. After making the products, I ran into a major problem: I did not know how to promote them.

How do I help people discover them? Once they do, how do I help someone understand that a product may be relevant to their life? These questions deserve more attention from me than simply adding another feature.

Fastlane entered my research at exactly this point. What interested me was its attempt to turn promotion into a workflow that can be run repeatedly.

![I shipped six apps and still struggled with marketing. What Fastlane made me reconsider. The original poster is bilingual.](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/01-shipped-six-apps.png)

## 01｜After Shipping, the Other Half of the Work Begins

In WonderElian’s “Along the Way” section, you can find Yixiu Meditation, Buer Within, Wendao, Xiazi, Style Atlas, and other work.[1]

I know why I made these products. Someone encountering one for the first time does not automatically share that context. They may not know what it is useful for, may not have the patience to read a full product page, or may not currently feel the need it addresses.

Promotion therefore has to answer a specific question: in what moment would someone remember this product?

A person whose mind will not stop at bedtime needs a different message, entry point, and reason from someone caught in a difficult relationship. A more complete feature list cannot replace that work.

## 02｜He Also Built Apps and Then Struggled to Be Seen

Fastlane co-founder Gaurav said in an interview that he had built several apps and then became stuck on marketing. He and his partners built a company around that recurring problem.[2]

![He built apps, then struggled to market them. Fastlane grew from that recurring problem. The original poster is bilingual.](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/02-marketing-bottleneck.png)

In an interview published on August 30, 2026, he reported that the software business had about $69,000 in monthly recurring revenue and more than 1,000 paying customers. These are founder-reported figures. They are not net profit and should not be read as current real-time revenue.[2]

Product Hunt confirms that Fastlane placed third for the day when it launched there on March 23, 2026.[3]

The case is commercially attractive, but Fastlane is a team venture. It should not be repackaged as proof that one person can casually build a tool and earn that amount every month. What matters more to me is that the company identified a problem I am also experiencing and will continue to face.

## 03｜How Does It Connect the Marketing Work?

Fastlane’s current website presents Fastlane v2 as a workflow coordinated by an AI agent named Senna. It understands a brand from its website, researches the market, generates creative assets, publishes content, and uses results to adjust the next batch.[4]

![Turn a product URL into a marketing workflow: understand, research, create, publish, and learn. The original poster is bilingual.](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/03-url-to-workflow.png)

The channels shown on its website include Meta, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts. This is the official capability range presented by the company; actual availability still depends on the plan, account connections, and specific features.[4]

My H5 product pages may be useful here. When answering a mobile-app developer on Product Hunt, the founder suggested providing a more information-rich website first.[3]

A URL is only the starting point, however. If the page offers a brand story without clearly identifying the user, the situation, and the product value, AI can only generate more material from vague input. I still have to explain who the product is for, what it helps with, and what someone can try next.

## 04｜The Design I Like Most: Begin with Choosing

In an early Fastlane demonstration, users could swipe through generated creative options and then schedule selected items for publication.[2]

![Generate first, then choose. Turn a blank page into a clearer decision. The original poster is bilingual.](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/04-generate-then-choose.png)

I find that design intelligent.

A blank editor asks me to decide the topic, opening, format, and expression all at once. Several prepared candidates let me begin with judgment: Does this sound like me? Is the idea clear? Would I be willing to publish it?

AI handles more of the initial production while the person keeps the final choice. That lowers the barrier to beginning marketing and gives taste, tone, and honest product communication a place in the workflow.

If I build my own promotion tool, I would seriously borrow this principle. The interface could be different. The essential point is to make it easier to complete one good publication.

## 05｜Why Can This Business Charge Repeatedly?

After an app launches, its value must still be explained, different messages need testing, and new people need to be reached. The need recurs naturally.

![Marketing recurs. Subscriptions, generation credits, and services are built around that need. The original poster is bilingual.](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/05-recurring-marketing.png)

As of October 14, 2026, the main plans displayed on the website were as follows. Prices are in U.S. dollars and exclude any applicable taxes:[4][5]

**Starter**: $29 monthly; $20 monthly equivalent on the annual plan; 500 credits per month.

**Growth**: $79 monthly; $55 monthly equivalent on the annual plan; 2,000 credits per month.

**Pro**: $199 monthly; $139 monthly equivalent on the annual plan; 10,000 credits per month.

The annual equivalents require payment for a full year and are not month-to-month prices. The website lists a static creative at 5 credits and a video at 60 credits. Starter is also limited to one social account and one campaign at a time.[4]

The business logic has three layers: a subscription for recurring use, credits for different levels of generation, and added services for customers who want more of the work handled for them.

Credits may also help control generation costs. Public information is not sufficient to calculate Fastlane’s actual gross margin, customer-acquisition cost, or churn. The revenue figure helps demonstrate demand; it does not show that the business is easy to run.

For my six apps, account, campaign, and workspace limits also matter. Paid distribution requires a separate media budget, while additional accounts and managed services add cost. The useful comparison is the total cost of completing an effective promotion cycle.

One trial detail deserves attention: the website describes a seven-day trial with 50 credits, while a video is listed at 60 credits. I should not assume the trial is enough to generate a video. The exact grant and access to video generation need confirmation before testing.[4]

## 06｜Its Way of Understanding Users Is Also Worth Studying

In the interview, the team described offering additional usage time in exchange for user calls, then organizing that feedback into product decisions.[2]

![Product direction comes from real use and the reasons people return. The original poster is bilingual.](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/06-real-direction.png)

For me, the useful lesson is to separate three observations: how people solve the problem today, how they actually use the product, and which people return over time and why.

“Do you like my product?” can easily produce a polite yes. Better questions are more specific: When did you last experience this problem? What did you do? Which step took the most effort?

If I eventually share my own promotion system, I want to observe how other people use it before rushing to add features I have only imagined.

## 07｜Which Parts of My Work Could It Handle?

Based on its public description, Fastlane aligns with part of my situation: I already have product websites, I need to create promotion continually, and I want to reduce the production and distribution burden.

![Six apps need more than one marketing message. Start with the real moment each product serves. The original poster is bilingual.](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/07-one-loop.png)

Its publicly listed channels are mainly global platforms. It does not currently present support for WeChat Official Accounts, WeChat Channels, Xiaohongshu, or Douyin. The global workflow may be worth testing; Chinese-market content and distribution still require separate validation.

Six apps also mean different user needs. Yixiu might begin with the question of how to take a short pause in the afternoon. Style Atlas might begin with why one image feels more ordered than another. These are messages I want to test, not growth findings that have already been proven.

AI can help produce assets, but the experience described must remain accurate. I should not promote a feature that has not shipped or use invented customer praise as evidence. Fastlane’s terms also require human review and state that generated content is not guaranteed to be fully unique or free from third-party rights issues.[5]

High-view examples on the website are appealing. For my apps, the more useful questions are whether someone enters the H5 experience, completes a meaningful action, downloads the app, or pays. Views are only one stage of that path.

## 08｜If I Build My Own, I Want to Begin with One Small Loop

My instinct is to meet my own need first, make the workflow genuinely useful, and then share it with people facing a similar problem.

![I want to build a promotion system I can truly use: one app, one channel, one real feedback loop. The original poster is bilingual.](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/08-build-one-loop.png)

The first version can be small. Choose one app and one channel. Organize the product information. Let AI suggest several content directions. I select and revise one, schedule it, and bring the result back into the next round of topics.

The existing H5 pages can offer a low-friction entry point. Each piece of content can use a source-specific link so that visits and actual use can be observed. An App Store button click, a real download, an activation, and a payment are different events and must not be treated as the same number.

I also want to measure something else: how much work does this system actually save me each week? If it only produces a larger pile of material waiting for review and leaves me busier, it has not solved my problem.

Pricing should wait until recurring value exists. A subscription makes sense for someone who continually needs planning, generation, scheduling, and review. Someone who needs a single delivery occasionally may be better served by one-time pricing.

First make one path work. Then consider making it wider.

## 09｜I Want the People Who Need These Products to Find Them

Fastlane showed me a direction worth studying: between creation and promotion, there can be a way of working that is easier to sustain.

![Solve your own problem first. Refine it, then share it with people who need it. The original poster is bilingual.](/assets/notes/2026-10-14-fastlane-ai-marketing/09-refine-and-share.png)

I made these apps because I needed them and because I believe some problems in everyday life deserve thoughtful care. What I want to add now is a clearer way to introduce them to the right people.

Begin with my own pain point. Remove the difficulties I encounter in real use one by one. If the resulting system eventually helps people around me, I will be glad to share it.

I want to make the work, and I want the people who need it to see it.

This series uses the **Fractal Art style** recommended by [Xiazi Style Atlas](https://style-atlas.wonderelian.com/). Recursive branches, selection, and feedback loops represent product distribution and learning, making a complex promotion process easier to observe, choose, and improve.

### Sources

- [WonderElian: Along the Way](https://wonderelian.com/). The count of six published Apple apps was supplied by the author.
- [Starter Story: The Insanely Obvious Secret Behind This $69K/Month SaaS](https://www.starterstory.com/stories/the-insanely-obvious-secret-behind-this-69k-month-saas), published August 30, 2026. Revenue and customer figures are self-reported in the interview.
- [Product Hunt: Fastlane](https://www.producthunt.com/products/fastlane-3), for its launch record and public replies from the co-founder.
- [Fastlane official website](https://www.usefastlane.ai/), checked October 14, 2026 for features, prices, credits, and channels. Website demonstrations and customer examples do not guarantee individual results.
- [Fastlane Terms](https://www.usefastlane.ai/terms), for human-review, generated-content, and fee terms.
